title: CSRF on sku_search.php - Missing CSRF Token on Search Endpoint
impact:
While lower severity due to the read-only nature of search operations, CSRF on the search endpoint can:
- Enable reconnaissance attacks to map database contents
- Be used to perform searches containing sensitive queries
- Leak information about user search patterns and interests
- Violate user privacy if searches contain sensitive business terms
- Demonstrate systematic security gaps in CSRF protection across all endpoints
- Be chained with IDOR vulnerabilities to exfiltrate confidential SKU data
- Leave unauthorized searches in browser history and server logs
- Facilitate social engineering attacks by gathering intelligence about the database
evidence:
Source code analysis of sku_search.php shows:
1. No CSRF token validation in POST request handler
2. No session token verification
3. No Referer/Origin header checking
4. No authorization checks
5. Direct use of $_POST['search'] parameter

The template (sku_search.twig) contains a form without CSRF token:
```html
<form method="post" action="sku_search.php">
    <input type="text" name="search" required>
    <button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>
```

Attack Scenario:
1. Attacker creates a malicious HTML page with hidden CSRF form
2. Attacker tricks authenticated user into visiting the page
3. User's browser automatically submits POST request to sku_search.php
4. Session cookie is automatically included in the request
5. Search executes on behalf of attacker without user knowledge
6. Attacker could exfiltrate search results via data exfiltration techniques

POC includes HTML demonstration file showing form-based CSRF attack, XMLHttpRequest attack vectors, and bypass techniques.
references:
CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
OWASP: CSRF Prevention Cheat Sheet
